title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which scammers used AI-generated images and videos to create a false online persona of a real, named attorney. The synthetic media was distributed across multiple social media platforms as the entry point, with victims then moved to WhatsApp for payment. The failure did not occur inside a legitimate AI product deployment; it occurred because generative tools capable of producing convincing likenesses were used offensively, outside any sanctioned system, to exploit the trust that a known professional's identity carries.

The scale visible in the takedown figures, roughly 6,500 fraudulent profiles across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, shows that platform-level detection did not catch the content before it reached victims. The fraud came to light not through automated moderation but because real clients contacted the genuine attorney's office after seeing the fake advertisements. That gap between the content going live and its removal represents the window in which financial harm occurred.

What is not established is the identity of the perpetrators, the total financial losses across all victims, or whether any platform had prior knowledge of the campaign before the attorney's anti-piracy contractor began removal requests.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, says criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Scammers have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of Leal offering immigration services he never provides, such as securing US residency for $2,200 or helping detainees escape immigration detention. He discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office about services he never advertised.

The fraud has escalated dramatically over the past three months, with scammers directing victims through WhatsApp after viewing fake social media videos. Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that removed nearly 6,500 fraudulent profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. He warns immigrants to be cautious of requests for payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App, and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scams. Leal urges people to verify anyone offering legal services online before providing payment.
